precepts.text: Who will set scourges over my thoughts and the discipline of wisdom over my heart, that they spare me not for my ignorances? Wisdom of Solomon 6:17, the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline, and the care of discipline is love. Ephesians 6:11, put on the whole armour; if you are not studying you are not battling, only falling victim.
precepts.point: Romans 6:16-19: to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are. Fall into sin and you worship the devil in that moment; you cannot serve two masters. As ye yielded your members to uncleanness, now yield them to righteousness unto holiness. Satan says you fell and cannot get up; you can repent, that is why Christ came.
precepts.why:
The hasty man needs control, and control comes by discipline: “Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins.” We have to learn discipline so we do not end up looking crazy out here.

“For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; and the care of discipline is love.” The very true beginning of following after wisdom is the desire of discipline. So we have to fight temptation, fight off the devil and overcome the beast in order to learn that discipline.

“Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” We have to put on all of the armour. If you are not studying, you are not battling; you are just falling victim.

Keeping God’s commandments does not give instant gratification. The consequences are delayed: we are going to get the kingdom. Sin gives you the pleasure right then and there, the instant dopamine, and once you are hardened by the deceitfulness of sin you no longer see any reason to keep God’s commandments because they do nothing for you in the moment. In this truth you have to self-motivate. You cannot wait for somebody else to give you a pep talk. You have to discipline your own soul if you want to make it.

precepts.text: The wife that brings in an heir by another disobeys the law of the Most High and leaves her memory to be cursed; that standard is why Judah called for judgment.
precepts.point: Then she produced the signet, bracelets, and staff, and Judah acknowledged them: She hath been more righteous than I, because that I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.
precepts.why:
“Thus shall it go also with the wife that leaveth her husband, and bringeth in an heir by another. For first, she hath disobeyed the law of the most High; and secondly, she hath trespassed against her own husband; and thirdly, she hath played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man.” Such a woman “shall be brought out into the congregation, and inquisition shall be made of her children”; her children “shall not take root”, and “She shall leave her memory to be cursed, and her reproach shall not be blotted out.”

That is the standard behind Judah’s judgment. Tamar was promised in the covenant, to Shelah; a woman promised in the covenant that plays the harlot and brings an heir by another has disobeyed the law of the Most High, and her reproach is not blotted out. So when Judah heard she was with child by whoredom, the judgment was heavy: “Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.”

Then she produced the signet, bracelets and staff, and Judah had to acknowledge them: “She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.” The fault ran back to him, for not performing what he had promised. “And he knew her again no more.”

precepts.text: The eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun; you cannot hide from him.
precepts.point: The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. When leadership corrects you, do not think evil of them: the Lord did not have to send leadership, he could have sent evil your way instead; correction is the warning and the mercy.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

precepts.why:
“Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.” The manpleaser fears the eyes of men; the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, and they consider the most secret parts. You cannot hide from him.

So make confession unto him. The Lord gives a dispensation of time and grace to get the mind right, to repent, pray, and fast over what we struggle with; the just man falleth seven times and riseth up again.

precepts.text: A humble man asks the Most High to scourge his thoughts and discipline his heart when he errs, so his ignorance does not increase and his sins abound to his destruction.
precepts.point: The people of the land slay the conspirators and make Josiah his son king in his stead. A sentence not executed speedily set his heart to do more evil, and his sins abounded to his own destruction.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
“O Lord, Father and Governor of all my whole life, leave me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them. Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins”. A humble man asks the Most High to scourge his thoughts and discipline his heart when he errs, so his ignorance does not increase and his sins do not abound to his destruction.

Amon never asked. He “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as did Manasseh his father”, sacrificing “unto all the carved images which Manasseh his father had made”, “And humbled not himself before the Lord, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; but Amon trespassed more and more.”

His sins abounded to his own destruction: “his servants conspired against him, and slew him in his own house.” The people of the land slew the conspirators “and made Josiah his son king in his stead.”

precepts.point: They scope you out in the daytime, marking your house, then come back at nighttime to hit you. For the morning is to them as the shadow of death; if one knows them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
Job says, “The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face.” Ecclesiasticus describes that same man: “All bread is sweet to a whoremonger, he will not leave off till he die. A man that breaketh wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the most High will not remember my sins”.

“Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.” The adulterer, and those who scope you out in the daytime, mark your house and come back at night to dig through it, know not the light; they only fear the eyes of men. But the Lord beholds all the ways of men and considers the most secret parts. That is why the morning is to them as the shadow of death: if one know them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.

precepts.text: A cry to have discipline set over your thoughts, lest ignorance increase to destruction and you commit that great transgression.
precepts.point: Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me; then shall I be upright and innocent from the great transgression. A sin addiction has to be replaced with a righteous addiction, because change does not just up and happen when you are accustomed to doing evil.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me”. Here is the same cry: “O Lord, Father and Governor of all my whole life, leave me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them. Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins”.

It is a cry to have discipline set over your thoughts, “Lest mine ignorances increase, and my sins abound to my destruction, and I fall before mine adversaries, and mine enemy rejoice over me”. Ignorance left alone increases to destruction, and that is how you commit the great transgression.

“Turn away from me vain hopes and concupiscence, and thou shalt hold him up that is desirous always to serve thee. Let not the greediness of the belly nor lust of the flesh take hold of me; and give not over me thy servant into an impudent mind.” A sin addiction has to be replaced with a righteous addiction, because change does not just up and happen when you are accustomed to doing evil. Ask for the scourges over your thoughts, and sins will not have dominion over you.

precepts.text: The adulterer thinks no one sees, but the eyes of the Most High are ten thousand times brighter than the sun and he shall be punished where he suspected not.
precepts.point: Jealousy is the rage of a man; in the day of vengeance he will spare nothing and regard no ransom. Let a husband find out his wife has been cheating and inquire the matter, and he may well put that brother to death once he catches up to him.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
“But whoso committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding: he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul. A wound and dishonour shall he get; and his reproach shall not be wiped away.” Ecclesiasticus lays out the adulterer's mind: “A man that breaketh wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the most High will not remember my sins”.

He thinks no one sees. “Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.” The eyes of the Most High are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, and the walls do not cover anything from him. “All bread is sweet to a whoremonger, he will not leave off till he die.”

Then the end: “This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and where he suspecteth not he shall be taken.” That is the wound and dishonour. Jealousy is the rage of a man, and in the day of vengeance he spares nothing and regards no ransom: let a husband find out his wife has been cheating and inquire the matter, and he may well put that brother to death once he catches up to him. He is taken where he suspected not.

precepts.text: The eyes of the Most High are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men.
precepts.point: The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Such a man only feareth the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.”

Sapphira feared the eyes of men and kept the story straight for them. But the eyes of the Most High behold all the ways of men and consider the most secret parts, and the agreement she made with her husband was not secret to him.

moments.label: Shapen in Iniquity: Resetting the Nervous System

points: Turn away from me vain hopes and concupiscence. Definition read in class: concupiscent describes a feeling of intense, powerful desire. It is strong.

Let not the greediness of the belly, nor lust of the flesh, take hold of me. This is the prayer: do not let my lustful appetite overtake me and destroy me. That is how we have to pray, honestly, with supplication, because we know what we deal with.

Satan comes in secrecy, when you are by yourself. When you are at the Sabbath, you are cool; everybody is watching, so there is no room to do anything wicked. But when you leave, that lust that is internal starts to mess with your mind, because now you are not around people that will hold you accountable.

A hot mind is as a burning fire, it will never be quenched till it be consumed: that is the inclination to sin, that concupiscence. All bread is sweet to a whoremonger: that dopamine he has to have. Speaking from experience of the old life: the men who stayed in the club until the lights came on were not there for a good time; that lifestyle is a chase that never satisfies.
